name: Tessera Corponation Dermal Cipher Lattice — 'The Palimpsest'
product_name: Tessera Corponation Dermal Cipher Lattice — 'The Palimpsest'
description: The Palimpsest is a subdermal data storage and encryption implant woven into the hypodermis across the upper back and shoulders, forming an invisible grid of bio-compatible polymer filaments embedded with crystalline memory nodes. Data is written to the lattice via a proprietary near-field induction handshake and is stored in distributed shards across the filament network, meaning no single point of extraction yields a readable payload. The system encrypts on write using a biometric key derived from the host's unique galvanic skin response signature — rendering data literally unreadable if removed from the living body.

cultural_context: In GLMZ's courier underground, carrying a Palimpsest is a mark of serious professional standing — it signals that you move data worth protecting with your life, because your life literally protects it. Street-level data runners who can't afford the implant sometimes fake the reputation, wearing decorative shoulder tattoos that mimic the faint subcutaneous texture the lattice produces. Among corporate security divisions, the Palimpsest has generated an ugly counter-industry: interrogation specialists who know how to keep a host alive and compliant long enough to force a biometric unlock.

Fixer intermediaries handling sensitive client contracts
'Dead drop' specialists in the Tessera contractor network
story_hooks: A courier arrives at the party's door, barely alive, with no ID and a Palimpsest full of data someone clearly killed to suppress — the biometric lock means only she can open it, if she survives.
A client hires the crew to retrieve a Palimpsest intact from a corporate safe house — the previous owner is deceased, and the data is now locked forever unless Tessera's master key exists somewhere.
One of the players discovers their own back feels wrong after a blackout — someone installed a Palimpsest on them without consent, and something is already written to it.
A Tessera insider offers to sell the galvanic spoofing tool that can fake a biometric unlock — but the device is a prototype, and Tessera wants it back badly enough to send cleaners.
